title: Smaller Filter, Same Phosphate Out
endLine: As filtration falls, a larger share must leave, or blood phosphate rises.

scenes.tts: The first film followed calcium through the kidney's filter: a huge daily flow, and a small share lost. Phosphate passes the same filter. Picture a healthy kidney and a badly failing one. In round numbers, both excrete eight hundred milligrams of phosphate a day. So why is blood phosphate high in the failing one?
scenes.caption: The first film followed calcium through the kidney's filter: a huge daily flow, and a small share lost. Phosphate passes the same filter. Picture a healthy kidney and a badly failing one. In round numbers, both excrete 800 mg of phosphate a day. So why is blood phosphate high in the failing one?
scenes.narration: The first film followed calcium through the kidney's filter: a huge daily flow, and a small share lost. Phosphate passes the same filter. Picture a healthy kidney and a badly failing one. In round numbers, both excrete 800 mg of phosphate a day. So why is blood phosphate high in the failing one?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's 16:9 world and colour map, now for phosphate instead of calcium. COLOUR BY CONCEPT, as before: BLUE = filtered load; GREEN = reabsorbed, back into the blood; ORANGE = excreted in urine; PURPLE = PTH; GREY = tissues and outlines. New in this film: MAGENTA = FGF23; TAN = calcitriol; WHITE = the plasma phosphate gauge. THE WORLD, kept all film, at most 6 things: (1) top left, a gut inlet arrow into plasma labelled 'from gut: 800 mg/day'; (2) left, a kidney filter drawn as a sieve whose mouth width is proportional to filtration rate, labelled 'filtration: 180 L/day'; (3) centre, the first film's horizontal filtered-load bar, its length proportional to the day's filtered phosphate, split into a GREEN reabsorbed part and an ORANGE excreted part at the right end; (4) under the bar, an ORANGE counter 'urine: 800 mg/day'; (5) right, a tall WHITE vertical gauge 'plasma phosphate (mg/dL)', 0 to 12, ticks every 2, with a faint shaded reference mark at 3.3 labelled 'healthy'. BAR SCALE, computed from the lesson's values, filtered load = filtration x 0.9 x plasma phosphate: 5,333 mg/day = 9 frame units wide, so the ORANGE 800 mg part is always 1.35 units wide. Small tag under the bar: 'round numbers, steady state'. Opening (on 'the first film'): a faint ghost of the first film's long BLUE calcium bar with its thin ORANGE sliver appears in the bar's place, tagged 'calcium, last time', then fades, and the phosphate bar grows in its place: 9 units, GREEN 85 percent, ORANGE 15 percent; small BLUE dots stream from the plasma through the sieve. On 'a healthy kidney and a badly failing one', the frame splits briefly into two half-height copies: left copy as above, gauge needle at 3.3; right copy with the sieve mouth narrowed to one twelfth, the bar shrunk to 1.35 units and entirely ORANGE, gauge needle at 5.9 glowing. Both ORANGE counters read 'urine: 800 mg/day' and pulse together on 'eight hundred'. On the question, the right copy's gauge needle shakes; WHITE text across the top: 'Same output. Why higher phosphate?'

The split frame merges back into the single healthy world (sieve at 180 L/day, 9-unit bar, needle at 3.3). Title 'Smaller Filter, Same Phosphate Out' fades in above the bar for 2 seconds while the question text fades out. BLUE dots keep streaming through the sieve; GREEN dots return to plasma; a few ORANGE dots drip to the urine counter.

scenes.tts: First, phosphate's controls. P T H throws phosphate out, but calcium sets P T H. So bone makes phosphate its own brake, F G F twenty-three. It acts on the kidney through a co-receptor, Klotho.
scenes.caption: First, phosphate's controls. PTH throws phosphate out, but calcium sets PTH. So bone makes phosphate its own brake, FGF23. It acts on the kidney through a co-receptor, Klotho.
scenes.narration: First, phosphate's controls. PTH throws phosphate out, but calcium sets PTH. So bone makes phosphate its own brake, FGF23. It acts on the kidney through a co-receptor, Klotho.
scenes.visual: On 'P T H throws phosphate out', a PURPLE token labelled 'PTH' (as in the first film) slides to the GREEN/ORANGE boundary on the bar; the ORANGE part of the bar pulses. On 'calcium sets P T H', a thin PURPLE thread runs from the token off-frame to a tiny tag 'set by calcium'. On 'bone makes', a GREY bone block rises into the bottom-left corner beside the sieve, labelled 'bone'; a MAGENTA token labelled 'FGF23' buds from it. On 'Klotho', the MAGENTA token docks at the GREEN/ORANGE boundary on the bar, where a small MAGENTA ring labelled 'Klotho' lights. No molecular structures: tokens are rounded chips.

scenes.tts: There it does two things. Like P T H, it lowers phosphate reabsorption in the proximal tubule. Unlike P T H, it lowers calcitriol, which cuts the phosphate absorbed from the gut.
scenes.caption: There it does two things. Like PTH, it lowers phosphate reabsorption in the proximal tubule. Unlike PTH, it lowers calcitriol, which cuts the phosphate absorbed from the gut.
scenes.narration: There it does two things. Like PTH, it lowers phosphate reabsorption in the proximal tubule. Unlike PTH, it lowers calcitriol, which cuts the phosphate absorbed from the gut.
scenes.visual: On 'lowers phosphate reabsorption', the boundary between GREEN and ORANGE on the bar ghost-shifts left (schematic, no number) and back; the PURPLE and MAGENTA tokens both glow, with a small tag 'both: less reabsorbed'. On 'lowers calcitriol', a TAN token labelled 'calcitriol' near the gut inlet dims and shrinks; the gut inlet arrow thins briefly (schematic) and the tag 'less from gut' appears beside it, then the arrow returns to its 800 mg/day width. A small PURPLE up-arrow beside the TAN token and a MAGENTA down-arrow show 'PTH: up' and 'FGF23: down'.

scenes.tts: Now the arithmetic, in round numbers. Phosphate excreted equals filtration, times filterable plasma phosphate, times the fraction excreted. A healthy filter passes one hundred eighty litres a day. Plasma phosphate of three point three milligrams per decilitre is thirty-three per litre, about ninety percent filterable: about thirty. Fifteen percent of the filtered phosphate leaves. One eighty times thirty, times fifteen percent, is about eight hundred.
scenes.caption: Now the arithmetic, in round numbers. Phosphate excreted equals filtration, times filterable plasma phosphate, times the fraction excreted. A healthy filter passes 180 L a day. Plasma phosphate of 3.3 mg/dL is 33 per litre, about 90 percent filterable: about 30. 15 percent of the filtered phosphate leaves. 180 times 30, times 15 percent, is about 800.
scenes.narration: Now the arithmetic, in round numbers. Phosphate excreted equals filtration, times filterable plasma phosphate, times the fraction excreted. A healthy filter passes 180 L a day. Plasma phosphate of 3.3 mg/dL is 33 per litre, about 90 percent filterable: about 30. 15 percent of the filtered phosphate leaves. 180 times 30, times 15 percent, is about 800.
scenes.visual: The hormone tokens shrink to small chips parked by the bone block. A WHITE equation strip appears above the bar, each term in the colour of the object it names: 'urine 800 =' (ORANGE) 'filtration' (GREY, matching the sieve label) 'x filterable phosphate' (WHITE) 'x fraction out' (ORANGE). Small tag beside it: 'filterable: about 90 percent'. On 'one hundred eighty litres', the sieve label pulses. On 'fifteen percent', the ORANGE part of the bar (15 percent of 9 units) pulses with the label '15%'. On 'three point three', the WHITE needle settles on 3.3 and the reference mark brightens. Computed: 180 x 0.9 x 33 mg/L x 0.15 = 800 mg/day. As the numbers are spoken, the equation strip fills in: '3.3 mg/dL = 33 mg/L', then '0.9 x 33 ≈ 30 mg/L', then '180 L x 30 mg/L x 0.15 ≈ 800 mg/day'.

scenes.tts: Here is the rule. At steady state, the kidneys must excrete the phosphate the gut absorbs. When filtration falls, the fraction excreted must rise. Where the fraction falls short, plasma phosphate rises instead.
scenes.caption: Here is the rule. At steady state, the kidneys must excrete the phosphate the gut absorbs. When filtration falls, the fraction excreted must rise. Where the fraction falls short, plasma phosphate rises instead.
scenes.narration: Here is the rule. At steady state, the kidneys must excrete the phosphate the gut absorbs. When filtration falls, the fraction excreted must rise. Where the fraction falls short, plasma phosphate rises instead.
scenes.visual: On 'excrete the phosphate the gut absorbs', the gut inlet label 'from gut: 800 mg/day' and the ORANGE counter 'urine: 800 mg/day' pulse together and a WHITE equals sign appears between them. On 'filtration falls', a ghost sieve narrows; on 'fraction excreted must rise', the ORANGE fraction label swells; on 'plasma phosphate rises instead', the WHITE needle ghost-lifts and drops back to 3.3. Label under the world, held to the end of the film: 'in = out: share up, or level up'.

scenes.tts: Cut filtration to sixty litres a day, a third of normal. At fifteen percent, phosphate must triple: three point three times three is about nine point nine. If F G F twenty-three and P T H push the fraction to fifty percent, about three is enough.
scenes.caption: Cut filtration to 60 L a day, a third of normal. At 15 percent, phosphate must triple: 3.3 times 3 is about 9.9. If FGF23 and PTH push the fraction to 50 percent, about 3.0 is enough.
scenes.narration: Cut filtration to 60 L a day, a third of normal. At 15 percent, phosphate must triple: 3.3 times 3 is about 9.9. If FGF23 and PTH push the fraction to 50 percent, about 3.0 is enough.
scenes.visual: On 'sixty litres', the sieve mouth narrows to one third; label 'filtration: 60 L/day'. On 'at fifteen percent', the WHITE needle climbs to 9.9 (computed: 800 / (60 x 0.9 x 0.15) = 98.8 mg/L); the bar stays 9 units long (filtered load is again 5,333 mg/day) with the ORANGE part at 1.35 units. On 'push the fraction to fifty percent', the MAGENTA and PURPLE chips slide to the GREEN/ORANGE boundary on the bar and glow; the bar shrinks to 2.7 units (1,600 mg/day), half GREEN and half ORANGE; the ORANGE part keeps its 1.35-unit width and never changes size. The needle falls to 3.0 (computed: 29.6 mg/L). The ORANGE counter still reads 800 mg/day. On 'must triple', a WHITE line beside the gauge reads '1/3 the filtration → 3 x the level: 3.3 x 3 ≈ 9.9'; on 'fifty percent', it changes to '800 ÷ (60 x 0.9 x 0.5) ≈ 30 mg/L = 3.0 mg/dL'.

scenes.tts: So moderate kidney disease keeps phosphate normal largely by raising the fraction. In one large cohort, F G F twenty-three was high while phosphate and P T H were still normal. That fits it rising first, without proving the order.
scenes.caption: So moderate kidney disease keeps phosphate normal largely by raising the fraction. In one large cohort, FGF23 was high while phosphate and PTH were still normal. That fits it rising first, without proving the order.
scenes.narration: So moderate kidney disease keeps phosphate normal largely by raising the fraction. In one large cohort, FGF23 was high while phosphate and PTH were still normal. That fits it rising first, without proving the order.
scenes.visual: On 'raising the fraction', the '50%' ORANGE label pulses. On 'one large cohort', three small level bars appear above the gauge, labelled 'FGF23' (MAGENTA, high), 'phosphate' (WHITE, normal) and 'PTH' (PURPLE, normal); schematic, no numbers. On 'without proving the order', a small arrow 'FGF23 first?' appears between the MAGENTA bar and the others, with a question mark that stays; then the three bars fade.

scenes.tts: Now cut filtration to fifteen litres a day. Suppose the kidney excreted every milligram it filtered. Could plasma phosphate stay normal?
scenes.caption: Now cut filtration to 15 L a day. Suppose the kidney excreted every milligram it filtered. Could plasma phosphate stay normal?
scenes.narration: Now cut filtration to 15 L a day. Suppose the kidney excreted every milligram it filtered. Could plasma phosphate stay normal?
scenes.visual: On 'fifteen litres', the sieve mouth narrows to one twelfth of the healthy width; label 'filtration: 15 L/day'. On 'every milligram', the GREEN part of the bar drains to nothing, leaving only the ORANGE 1.35-unit block labelled '100% out'. The WHITE needle is hidden behind a question mark. Question card across the top in white: 'Can phosphate stay normal?'
Predict pause. The question card stays. Thin streams of BLUE dots still pass the narrow sieve and all turn ORANGE; No other change. The gauge question mark pulses slowly. No numbers appear.

scenes.tts: No. The fraction cannot pass one hundred percent. Even there, eight hundred milligrams divided by fifteen litres, ninety percent filterable, is about fifty-nine per litre. That is five point nine per decilitre. At fifty percent, the level must double, to about eleven point nine.
scenes.caption: No. The fraction cannot pass 100 percent. Even there, 800 mg divided by 15 L, 90 percent filterable, is about 59 per litre. That is 5.9 mg/dL. At 50 percent, the level must double, to about 11.9.
scenes.narration: No. The fraction cannot pass 100 percent. Even there, 800 mg divided by 15 L, 90 percent filterable, is about 59 per litre. That is 5.9 mg/dL. At 50 percent, the level must double, to about 11.9.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves. On 'cannot pass one hundred percent', a RED stop line appears at the right edge of the ORANGE block, labelled 'ceiling: 100%'. On 'five point nine', the question mark lifts and the WHITE needle rises to 5.9 (computed: 800 / (15 x 0.9 x 1.0) = 59.3 mg/L), well above the 'healthy' mark at 3.3. On 'fifty percent', a ghost bar grows to 2.7 units, half GREEN and half ORANGE, and a ghost needle rises to 11.9 (computed: 118.5 mg/L), then both ghosts fade back to the 100 percent case. As the 5.9 is reached, a WHITE line beside the gauge reads '800 ÷ (15 x 0.9 x 1.0) ≈ 59 mg/L = 5.9 mg/dL'; on 'must double', it adds '÷ 0.5 → 11.9'.

scenes.tts: So phosphate settles high, and climbs from there. Calcitriol falls and P T H rises, yet phosphate stays up. P T H's usual signature, calcium up and phosphate down, fails here.
scenes.caption: So phosphate settles high, and climbs from there. Calcitriol falls and PTH rises, yet phosphate stays up. PTH's usual signature, calcium up and phosphate down, fails here.
scenes.narration: So phosphate settles high, and climbs from there. Calcitriol falls and PTH rises, yet phosphate stays up. PTH's usual signature, calcium up and phosphate down, fails here.
scenes.visual: The WHITE needle creeps slowly upward from 5.9 (direction only, schematic). On 'calcitriol falls', the TAN token dims; on 'P T H rises', the PURPLE chip grows and glows at the GREEN/ORANGE boundary on the bar. On 'usual signature', a PURPLE card appears beside the gauge: 'PTH: calcium up, phosphate down'; on 'fails here', the whole card receives a RED cross while the needle stays high. The ORANGE counter still reads 800 mg/day.

scenes.tts: A smaller filter can be covered by sending out a larger share. When the share can grow no more, the blood level has to give.
scenes.caption: A smaller filter can be covered by sending out a larger share. When the share can grow no more, the blood level has to give.
scenes.narration: A smaller filter can be covered by sending out a larger share. When the share can grow no more, the blood level has to give.
scenes.visual: Recap in the same world, quickly and computed: the sieve widens back to 180 L/day, then steps down to 60 and 15. With each step the bar shrinks around the fixed ORANGE 1.35-unit block (9, then 2.7 units half ORANGE, then all ORANGE), and the WHITE needle reads 3.3, then 3.0, then 5.9. On 'the blood level has to give', the needle at 5.9 glows and the label 'in = out: share up, or level up' brightens.

End card over the dimmed but still moving world (BLUE dots passing the narrow sieve, ORANGE dots dripping to the urine counter at 800 mg/day). Large white text, centred: 'As filtration falls, a larger share must leave, or blood phosphate rises.'
